The game is fine, what you see on the store page is exactly what you get. But look, I was promised a menhera and this one is pretty tame. It almost feels like they didn't want to scare away normies who can't handle anything beyond the most generic tropes. There are western women who behave worse than this IN PUBLIC and I'm supposed to react to a girl with severe trust issues who likes being by the ocean and hates camping? She isn't even wrong, ♥♥♥♥ camping! The presentation is great. The gameplay can be slow though. I didn't mind the dice rolling speed but with a good build you can beat each day really fast and you spend a lot of time skipping text you have already seen. The most fun I had was with a healing build and I gave her triple health, I was almost impossible to kill and it took about 15 minutes to win that day. It felt like an actual game where choosing when to reroll or take the damage mattered. The main selling point is the girl and I found the menhera experience to be underwhelming. If you only care about gameplay I say you should give it a shot, it isn't bad.

The game feels incomplete. Why? Well... On its own merit, the fundamental premise and thematic of this game is very interesting. So had high expectations. But it turns out the game is one dimensional and very boring. There is no way to survive, escape, or defeat your opponents. You can basically tune out Menhera-Chan and get the same experience. There is no story to explore. There is no progression. The is no meaning. As it stands... if you need something to waste time with it's perfect but don't expect anything else. In my first run I got 19 out of 40 challenges from the story mode. Including a rare one called "Obvious cheating" which is ironic considering I did even notice or realize, lmao! Hopefully they will ad real story progression or at least add in a few different ways to win without hiding it behind a dlc. Oh! Another way I can put it more simply. Once you play the game. Then that's it there is nothing to talk about or share. It leaves a lacking impression. Like it was hyping it's self up then... nothing. "Oh this is really it? No secrets or anything? No conflict? No retaliation? Or negotiation? Nothing? Really nothing?!". Like I said before you can ignore the dialogue and or just watch a stream of it and still get the same experience. or better (depending on who your streamer is).

Every star observed, every blade of grass touched, and every word spoken does not exist to you in the external void, but as a simulated spark within the theater of your own consciousness. The universe you navigate is not the raw, objective world itself, but a meticulous reconstruction painted entirely by your mind. To experience anything is to experience the mind's interpretation of it. Your joys, your terrors, your victories, and your losses do not happen *to* you; they happen *within* you. You have never truly touched the outer world—only the nerve endings that translate it, and the consciousness that animates it. Ultimately, you do not live in a universe. You live in a reality of your own construction, making you both the architect and the sole inhabitant of everything you will ever know.

Menherarium is a tense deck-building roguelite where every dice roll costs blood. Twisted rules, cheat cards, and a clingy menace make each 7-day run thrilling and unsettling. Will you win?
Clever dice-based strategy and sharp voice acting make battles engaging, but uneven balance, repetitive depth, and muddled storytelling hold back this bold gambling-tactics hybrid.
